papers.abstract: Complete (R0) resection remains the primary surgical objective for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM), but margin width cannot be interpreted independently of tumor anatomy, biology, and the amount of functional liver sacrificed to obtain it. This focused narrative review re-examines surgical margins from the perspective of parenchymal preservation and longitudinal multimodal treatment. We distinguish parenchymal R1 exposure (R1par), an undesirable transection-surface event consistently associated with local recurrence in retrospective series, from planned vascular R1 detachment (R1vasc), which has shown more favorable outcomes than R1par in selected retrospective series but remains dependent on careful anatomical selection. Vessel-skeletonized parenchymal-sparing hepatectomy (VESPAH) is presented as one operative model for achieving complete macroscopic clearance while preserving intrahepatic vascular architecture; the evidence for this model is confined to retrospective series and is therefore illustrative and hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. We further propose “treatment continuity”—preservation of the physiological and anatomical capacity to receive indicated systemic therapy and repeat local treatment—as a reportable surgical outcome. A four-axis framework integrating technical resectability, functional reserve, tumor biology, and future treatment options is outlined, together with a minimum set of reporting elements for margin phenotype and operational definitions for four candidate measures of treatment continuity. R0 resection should remain the goal, but the quality of hepatectomy for CRLM may be more comprehensively assessed by considering both the margin achieved at the index operation and the treatments that remain feasible thereafter.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The prognostic significance of residual ductal carcinoma in situ (ypTis) compared with no residual tumor in the breast (ypT0) after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) remains uncertain. We compared clinicopathological, MRI, treatment, and survival outcomes between these groups. Methods: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients with stage II–III breast cancer who achieved ypN0 and ypT0/is status after NAC and definitive surgery between 2019 and 2023. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with ypTis. DFS and OS were assessed using Kaplan–Meier analysis and log-rank tests. Results: Among 175 patients, 139 (79.4%) had ypT0 and 36 (20.6%) had ypTis. Median follow-up was 51 months. Clinical T-stage distribution differed significantly between groups (p = 0.010), with cT4 disease in 13.9% of ypTis versus 2.2% of ypT0 patients. HER2 positivity and MRI-detected satellite foci were more frequent in the ypTis group. In multivariable analysis, HER2 positivity (OR 2.50, 95% CI 1.05–5.93; p = 0.038), and MRI-detected satellite foci (OR 2.41, 95% CI 1.12–5.16; p = 0.024) were associated with ypTis. Local recurrence occurred in 3/36 (8.3%) ypTis and 1/139 (0.7%) ypT0 patients. DFS did not differ significantly between groups (5-year estimates: 78.7% vs. 78.9%; p = 0.860). OS also showed no significant difference (5-year estimates: 96.8% vs. 87.3%; p = 0.320). Conclusions: Residual DCIS was not associated with statistically significant differences in DFS or OS following NAC. However, these findings do not establish prognostic equivalence and should be interpreted cautiously given the limited number of ypTis patients and outcome events.

papers.abstract: Background: Early gastric cancer (EGC) lacks a predictive tool integrating endoscopic therapy (ET), gastrectomy (G), and chemoradiotherapy (CRT) to support individualized risk stratification. This study compared cancer-specific survival (CSS) and overall survival (OS) across the four treatment strategies and developed and externally validated a CSS prediction model incorporating oncologic characteristics and treatment strategy (presented as a nomogram and online tool). Methods: In a U.S. cohort (2017–2021), 1766 patients with EGC were classified into four treatments groups (ET, ET + CRT, G, G + CRT); an independent multicenter cohort (n = 1333) provided external validation. Kaplan–Meier curves, log-rank tests, and Cox regression assessed unadjusted differences, with confounding balanced by stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (sIPTW). Predictors were selected by univariable Cox, LASSO, Boruta, and best-subset regression; performance was evaluated by C-index, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. Results: After sIPTW adjustment, CSS did not differ significantly between ET and G (p = 0.856), whereas G was associated with better CSS than G + CRT (p < 0.05). In exploratory analyses of node-positive patients, G + CRT was associated with lower cancer-specific mortality than G alone (p < 0.05). The CSS prediction model was validated internally and externally (AUCs for 1-, 3-, and 5-year CSS: 0.769, 0.737, 0.717 internally; 0.943, 0.890, 0.872 externally). Conclusions: This is the first externally validated EGC CSS model integrating all four treatments. For eligible patients, ET was associated with survival comparable to G and superior to G + CRT; among node-positive patients, G + CRT was associated with lower mortality than G alone. The model supports individualized prediction and treatment decisions.

papers.abstract: Disease relapse remains the leading cause of treatment failure in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (allo-HCT). This narrative review, searched from Pubmed, from 2015 to 2026, critically synthesizes the available evidence on post-transplant maintenance strategies, which have evolved over the past three decades from conventional chemotherapy to molecularly targeted agents and interventions aimed at modulating antileukemic immunity. Particular attention is given to the biological rationale, efficacy, safety, and clinical applicability of these approaches, as well as to the substantial heterogeneity in study design, patient selection, and treatment initiation and duration. The available evidence indicates that the potential benefit of maintenance is unlikely to be uniform across all recipients and should be interpreted in relation to AML molecular features, baseline relapse risk, prior treatment exposure, measurable residual disease status, expected toxicity, and the patient’s overall clinical condition. Although selected strategies may prolong remission and improve survival, the optimal agent, timing, duration, and target population remain incompletely defined. Current evidence therefore supports a risk-adapted and molecularly informed approach, while underscoring the need for adequately powered prospective studies using standardized endpoints and incorporating quality-of-life outcomes.

papers.abstract: Background: Hepatic arterial infusion (HAI) chemotherapy for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) is delivered through a port–catheter system implanted percutaneously by interventional radiology or surgically. Previous studies have pooled device complications across access methods as event counts, but have not synthesised the technical performance and durability of fully percutaneous insertion at the patient level. Methods: Medline, EMBASE, Cochrane Library, Scopus and Web of Science were searched for studies published from 2000 onward reporting adults with CRLM undergoing HAI port insertion. Primary analyses were restricted to fully percutaneous implanted ports, using outcome-specific, patient-level numerators and denominators; a study using surgical arterial cutdown was added in sensitivity analyses. Risk of bias in the device outcomes was assessed at item level for patient selection, completeness of data, outcome ascertainment and selective reporting, with Cochrane RoB 2 used additionally for the single randomised trial. Random-effects proportion meta-analyses used the Freeman–Tukey double arcsine transformation and the DerSimonian–Laird estimator, with a binomial generalised linear mixed model (GLMM) as an alternative. Outcomes with inconsistent definitions or denominators were synthesised narratively. Results: Fifteen studies contributed 811 patients, 654 of whom underwent percutaneous insertion. One study was randomised, five prospective and nine retrospective; three reported a surgical comparator arm. Risk of bias in the device outcomes was low in one study, moderate in six and high in eight. Eleven studies (423 patients) of fully percutaneous implanted ports contributed to the primary analyses. Technical success was reported explicitly by eight and achieved in 276 of 278 patients (99.3%, exact 95% CI 97.4–99.9%); with only two failures, pooled models added little. Device-attributable definitive failure, meaning permanent discontinuation of HAI because of the device, occurred in 39 of 374 patients (crude 10.4%) over observation periods that varied widely; the random-effects estimate was 6.9% (95% CI 2.1–13.7%; I2 = 74.5%; GLMM 6.9%, 3.0–15.2%), and 11.6% (95% CI 6.3–18.0%) in the six studies at low or moderate risk of bias. Catheter dislodgement affected a pooled 5.8% (95% CI 1.6–11.6%), and 14.8% where the port was checked angiographically before every course or every four weeks; hepatic arterial occlusion affected 3.4% (95% CI 0.9–7.0%; four studies). Revision was required in 56% and 59% of percutaneous patients in the two series reporting it. Conclusions: Percutaneous insertion of HAI ports rarely failed technically in these series, but reintervention was common and permanent loss of HAI to a device problem within the follow-up reported was estimated at 6.9% in the primary analysis and 11.6% in studies at lower risk of bias, with more problems detected where the device was monitored more closely. Catheter-tip technique, follow-up duration and intensity of device surveillance are possible, unproven contributors to heterogeneity. These predominantly observational data support the feasibility of percutaneous access, not patient suitability for HAI chemotherapy.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Resection is the treatment goal in unresectable liver-limited metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). Anti-VEGF and anti-EGFR antibodies are effective in RAS wild-type mCRC, but the better option for conversion is unclear. We compared their efficacy and tolerability as first-line treatment. Methods: In this prospective, single-centre cohort study, patients with RAS-wild-type mCRC and unresectable liver metastases received cetuximab or panitumumab (anti-EGFR) or bevacizumab (anti-VEGF) with FOLFOX or FOLFIRI. We compared the overall response rate (ORR), depth of response (DoR), resection rate (RR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS) and toxicity, using Cox regression adjusted for baseline covariates. Results: Of 101 patients, 51 received anti-EGFR therapy and 50 bevacizumab. Anti-EGFR therapy achieved a higher ORR (70.6% vs. 50.0%; p = 0.034), deeper response (47.2% vs. 33.7%; p = 0.004) and higher RR (66.7% vs. 46.0%; p = 0.036). The median PFS was longer (12.1 vs. 8.5 months; adjusted HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.29–0.78; p = 0.003), whereas the median OS did not differ significantly (30.4 vs. 25.5 months; p = 0.382). Grade 3/4 toxicity was similar (35.3% vs. 22.0%; p = 0.187). Conclusions: Anti-EGFR therapy was associated with higher response and resection rates and longer PFS and may be considered when conversion is the aim; these single-centre, non-randomised findings require confirmation in randomised studies.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: While neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy has become a standard treatment for patients with early-stage triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) based on KEYNOTE-522, the trial did not directly compare neoadjuvant with adjuvant chemo-immunotherapy. We compared treatment patterns and survival outcomes between neoadjuvant and adjuvant chemo-immunotherapy in real-world settings. Methods: We identified women with clinical stage II–III TNBC diagnosed from 2017–2023 in the National Cancer Database (NCDB) who underwent definitive surgery and received chemo-immunotherapy. Factors associated with neoadjuvant treatment were evaluated. Overall survival (OS) was assessed using Kaplan–Meier curves, univariable and multivariable Cox regression, and propensity-score overlap weighting. Prespecified subgroup analyses were performed by clinical T and N stage. Results: Among 21,757 women, 21,340 received neoadjuvant and 417 received adjuvant chemo-immunotherapy. Higher clinical T stage, node-positive disease, and diagnosis in 2021–2023 were associated with neoadjuvant treatment. One-, 2-, and 3-year OS were 98.8%, 93.2%, and 88.6% with neoadjuvant versus 94.3%, 88.9%, and 81.6% with adjuvant chemo-immunotherapy, respectively. Neoadjuvant treatment was associated with improved OS in univariable analysis (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.46–0.72; p < 0.001), multivariable analysis (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.42–0.66; p < 0.001), and after overlap weighting (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.45–0.73; p < 0.001). Associations consistently favored neoadjuvant treatment across clinical T- and N-stage subgroups. Conclusions: In this retrospective NCDB study, neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy was associated with improved OS compared with adjuvant chemo-immunotherapy. These hypothesis-generating findings are consistent with current clinical practice but should be interpreted cautiously, as differences in treatment regimens and completion rates, which could not be assessed in the NCDB, may have contributed to the observed survival benefit.

papers.abstract: Background: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a global epidemic with extremely high lethality, yet its exact molecular mechanisms remain under-explored. Therefore, the study of molecular regulators of the developmental process of LUAD is of crucial importance for developing innovative therapeutic approaches to enhance the survival rate of individuals with LUAD. Methods: Through bioinformatics analyses of several public gene databases, we thoroughly examined the expression, clinical significance, co-expressed genes, and signal transduction pathways of CEACAM7 in LUAD. Reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) and Western blotting (WB) were utilized to detect the CEACAM7 expression in clinical LUAD tissues. The CCK-8 method, WB, colony formation, Transwell, wound healing, and immunoprecipitation assays were utilized to explore the molecular mechanism of CEACAM7′s role in LUAD. The tumorigenic role of CEACAM7 was further validated in vivo in a subcutaneous xenograft model established in female BALB/c nude mice (n = 5 per group). Results: CEACAM7 is significantly overexpressed in LUAD, and its upregulation is linked to tumor aggressiveness and poor prognosis. Our experimental results suggest that regulation of CEACAM7 expression, either through up- or down-regulation, results in enhancement or suppression of growth and invasion of H1650 cells, respectively. In H1650 cells, CEACAM7 was shown to directly interact with GCNT3 and trigger growth and invasion of H1650 cells and epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT). In vivo, knockdown of CEACAM7 significantly suppressed xenograft tumor growth in nude mice. Conclusions: Our findings demonstrating the biological function of CEACAM7 in LUAD both in vitro and in vivo provide new insights and underline its capability as a predictive biomarker and therapeutic target.

papers.abstract: Background: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) shows molecular heterogeneity that complicates prognosis and selection of therapy. Integration of upstream pathway activity and transcription factor (TF) regulatory networks with gene expression to define molecular subtypes remains underexplored. Methods: We harmonized integrative transcriptomics and regulatory data from 483 primary ccRCC tumors from TCGA, integrating PARADIGM pathway activity Z-scores, RABIT TF activity scores, and normalized mRNA expression. Molecular subtypes were identified using consensus clustering. Clusters were characterized using GSEA with MSigDB Hallmark gene sets, differential pathway and expression analyses, and multivariate Cox regression (adjusted for age, gender, and stage). External validation was performed using a survival-guided Random Forest classifier. Results: Consensus clustering identified two molecular subtypes (K = 2, stability = 0.957). Cluster 0 (proliferative-metabolic) (n = 154, 31.9%) was enriched for E2F Targets (NES = 2.140, FDR < 0.001), G2-M Checkpoint (NES = 1.548), and Cholesterol Homeostasis (NES = 1.645), with SREBF1 as the dominant TF driver (t = 11.53). Cluster 1 (angiogenic-immune) (n = 329, 68.1%) was enriched for Angiogenesis (NES = −1.816, FDR < 0.001), Inflammatory Response (NES = −1.623), and EMT (NES = −1.767), governed by IKZF1 (t = −13.15), SPI1 (t = −13.12), and FOS (t = −12.80). Differential expression identified 880 significant genes (FDR < 0.05, |Log2FC| > 1). Multivariate Cox regression confirmed cluster assignment as an independent prognostic factor (HR = 0.70, 95% CI 0.51–0.96, p = 0.026), with Cluster 1 associated with improved overall survival. External validation reproduced significant survival stratification (Log-Rank p = 1.66 × 10−2). Conclusions: Two biologically distinct ccRCC subtypes were defined by integrating regulatory networks with gene expression data, a proliferative-metabolic subtype with worse prognosis and an angiogenic-immune subtype with improved survival. This provides a network-informed transcriptomic framework for molecularly stratified decision-making for prognosis and therapeutics.

papers.abstract: The modern role of surgery in small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) is best understood as an unresolved question rather than a settled recommendation. Older randomized trials established that surgery has no role in unselected SCLC, but these trials predate PET-CT staging, endosonographic mediastinal staging, and immunotherapy, and therefore cannot answer today’s clinical question in modern, invasively staged, node-negative disease. Current guideline support for resection in cT1–2N0 SCLC rests largely on retrospective, registry-based data (SEER, NCDB) that carry substantial selection bias rather than randomized confirmation. Meanwhile, the nonsurgical comparator has advanced: chemo-radiotherapy plus durvalumab consolidation, validated in the ADRIATIC trial, now defines the modern limited-stage standard against which any surgical strategy must be benchmarked. Molecular subtyping (ASCL1, NEUROD1, POU2F3, inflamed phenotypes; TP53/RB1 co-alteration) and emerging neoadjuvant and perioperative chemo-immunotherapy data introduce plausible, though unproven, avenues for patient selection and treatment sequencing. Surgical tissue also offers a translational platform for studying immune microenvironment, clonal evolution, and treatment resistance. This review argues that surgery for SCLC is neither obsolete nor an established standard in isolation. Its future role requires two distinct lines of prospective investigation: comparisons of upfront surgery with neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy followed by resection, which address treatment sequencing, and comparisons of surgery-based multimodality treatment with definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy followed by durvalumab, which address the incremental value of surgery over contemporary nonsurgical care.

papers.abstract: Abstract Tumors display marked similarities with embryos, exploiting embryonic developmental programs. Beyond the embryo, the placenta also shares features with malignant tumors, such as invasion, immune evasion, and rapid nutrient exchange, highlighting the need for mechanistic investigations of tumor development through the lens of placental biology. In this study, by screening placental-specific genes with aberrant expression in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), we found that the paternally expressed gene 10 (PEG10, a retrovirus-like gene) was overexpressed in HCC and associated with poor patient prognosis. Liver-specific deletion of Peg10 significantly impeded hepatocarcinogenesis and tumor progression in a hydrodynamic tail vein injection–induced HCC mouse model. PEG10 drove tumor cells to co-opt the metabolic phenotype of trophoblast cells by upregulating key glucose metabolic regulators glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1) and hexokinase 2 (HK2). Mechanistically, as an RNA-binding protein, PEG10 inhibited the Staufen 1 (STAU1)–mediated mRNA decay (SMD) pathway, stabilizing GLUT1 and HK2 mRNA to enhance glucose uptake and aerobic glycolysis. Furthermore, retinoic acid pharmacologically suppressed PEG10 expression, effectively abrogating the adaptive metabolic advantage and acting synergistically with sorafenib to restrict tumor growth. Collectively, this study reveals how HCC aberrantly reactivates the placental gene PEG10 to orchestrate oncogenic glucose uptake and metabolism, identifying it as a compelling therapeutic target for metabolic intervention in cancer. Significance: Aberrant reactivation of the placental gene PEG10 drives tumor glucose uptake and metabolic reprogramming in hepatocellular carcinoma by inhibiting Staufen1-mediated mRNA decay, which may open avenues for targeting onco-fetal pathways in cancer.

papers.abstract: Background: Many clinicians monitor the abductor digiti minimi (ADM) muscle during surgery using electromyography (EMG) for ease and consistency of electrode placement, while practice guidelines recommend monitoring of responses at the adductor pollicis (AP) muscle. This study compared the onset time of rocuronium neuromuscular block and the sugammadex-induced recovery time recorded simultaneously from the AP and ADM muscles. Methods: In 44 consenting patients undergoing general anesthesia, simultaneous EMG recording of ADM and AP muscles was performed. Right- and left-hand selection of monitored muscle (AP vs . ADM) was randomized, and patients’ handedness was recorded. The primary outcomes were the onset time of neuromuscular block (administration of rocuronium until train-of-four [TOF] count equal to 0), recovery time (time from sugammadex administration until TOF ratio greater than or equal to 0.9), and time to maximal recovery (sugammadex administration until TOF ratio equal to 1.0). Results: There were no significant differences between ADM and AP measurements in onset time, recovery to TOF ratio greater than or equal to 0.9, or time to maximal recovery (TOF ratio equal to 1.0) between EMG responses recorded simultaneously from ADM and AP muscles. However, a difference in recovery times between ADM and AP existed, depending on which hand was monitored. When ADM was monitored on the right hand, the readings showed earlier recovery than AP, and the mean difference was 93 s (25% faster) and 105 s (20% faster) for time to TOF ratio greater than or equal to 0.9 and time to TOF ratio equal to 1.0, respectively. There was no difference between the AP and ADM muscles when monitoring was performed on the left hand. Conclusions: The current study underscores the equivalency between ADM and AP muscles for routine neuromuscular monitoring during surgery. When monitoring the nondominant arm, the ADM and AP muscles have similar recoveries. In the dominant arm, the ADM muscle recovery is significantly faster than that of the AP muscle.

papers.abstract: Abstract Caregivers of patients with cancer frequently coordinate care while navigating insurance, employment, financial, and benefits systems, yet their legal and administrative needs remain poorly characterized. We analyzed caregiver-initiated consultations in national non-profit organization’s Legal & Financial Navigation Program from 2021 to 2024. Among 1,091 consultations, caregivers were predominantly female (67.7%) and working age (19-64y, 60.8%); 10.9% lived in a different state than the patient. Caregivers reported 1,889 legal concerns, most commonly involving health insurance (32.1%), finances (24.0%), disability insurance (14.2%), and employment (11.8%). More than half (51.1%) reported multiple concurrent legal concerns. In adjusted analyses, residence in the South was associated with higher odds of multiple barriers than the Northeast (odds ratio [OR] = 1.60), whereas Marketplace, Medicaid, and Medicare coverage were associated with lower odds relative to employer-sponsored insurance. These findings support caregiver-focused screening, education, and legal navigation as components of supportive oncology care.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Screening is a key tool to improve colorectal cancer (CRC) outcomes and mitigate disparities, and reliable estimates of screening variation across communities can help prioritize screening interventions. However, existing screening surveillance infrastructure relies on labor-intensive telephone survey methodology. We aimed to develop novel methods of estimating CRC utilization for small geographic areas using North Carolina multi-payer claims data and to identify patterns and determinants of geographic variation in screening adherence. Methods Using data from the Cancer Information and Population Health Resource, a multi-payer claims database, we generated annual screen-eligible cohorts and identified screening procedures. We then used Bayesian spatial models to estimate screening adherence for 1180 zip-code-based small areal units. We used geographic contextual data to re-weight estimates from the insured to the total (uninsured + insured) population. We examined associations between area-level racial composition and screening adherence stratified by age and sex. Results Across all years, the observed proportion of person-years up-to-date among insured age-eligible adults statewide was 80.3%; among all age-eligible adults, 75.8% were estimated to be up-to-date. Model-estimated screening adherence in small areas ranged between 43.1% and 93.1%. Increasing Black racial composition was associated with lower screening adherence across all sexes and age strata. Older age and female sex were associated with higher screening adherence. Conclusions Model-based estimation of CRC adherence from insurance claims and geographic data is feasible at scale and yields comprehensive estimates at small-area levels. There is wide variation in community-level screening adherence, with many areas falling below public health targets.

papers.abstract: Abstract Dysbiosis after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (allo-HSCT) predisposes to acute gastrointestinal (GI) graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) are prebiotics that establish a favorable intestinal microbiome. We hypothesized that peritransplant HMOs would reduce dysbiosis, and conducted a prospective phase 1/2 study in which 70 patients received oral, daily 2’-fucosyllactose (2’-FL), the most abundant HMO, from start of conditioning through day +30. Primary phase 1 and phase 2 end points were safety and tolerability of 2′-FL and longitudinal preservation of microbiome diversity, respectively. Phase 1 and phase 2 patients with ≥60% adherence were evaluated by correlative analyses. Twenty-nine age-matched patients with available samples in our institutional biorepository served as contemporary controls. 2′-FL was safe and well tolerated on the phase 1 study, which established dosing for the phase 2 study. Shannon diversity was preserved in 2′-FL recipients and declined from baseline to day +30 in controls (P = .04). Generalized linear mixed model analysis revealed higher association of Bifidobacteria and Blautia with 2′-FL (adjusted P< .05). Higher fecal isoleucine (P = .005), tyrosine (P = .05), and taurine (P = .04) were observed in 2′-FL recipients, all associated with protection and regeneration of intestinal epithelium. Lower plasma regulatory islet-derived 3α (P = .053) and suppressor of tumorigenicity 2 levels (P = .038) were observed in 2′-FL recipients compared with controls. Incidence of grade II-IV acute GI GVHD was 0% in 2′-FL recipients compared with 17% in controls (P = .009). Adenovirus reactivation was 0% in 2′-FL recipients compared with 17% in controls (P = .009). 2′-FL is safe and modifies the gut microbiome in children after allo-HSCT. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as #NCT04263597.

papers.abstract: Abstract Direct targeting of the oncoprotein MYC has not yet been successful. Here we report a novel dual protein degrader, GT19630, which binds directly to MYC and G1 to S phase transition protein 1 (GSPT1). GT19630 disrupts a novel feedforward loop of MYC and GSPT1, in which MYC promotes transcription of GSPT1, and GSPT1 senses the stop codon of MYC to properly terminate its translation. The agent induces an integrated stress response and abrogates oxidative phosphorylation through inhibition of the tricarboxylic acid cycle, resulting in apoptosis. GT19630 has superior activity compared with GSPT1-targeting molecular glues. GT19630 induces profound antiproliferative effects and apoptosis at low nanomolar concentrations in a multitude of leukemia and lymphoma cell lines and primary samples, including those with TP53 mutations. GT19630 is highly active in vivo in models of therapy-resistant hematologic malignancies, including Burkitt lymphoma, acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and multiple myeloma. CD34+ AML blasts overexpress MYC protein compared with normal hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPCs), and GT19630 induces greater cytotoxicity in AML cells compared with normal HSPCs. Further, GT19630 restores sensitivity to venetoclax and profoundly prolongs survival in vivo in venetoclax-resistant AML. GT19630 was well tolerated in humanized Crbn mice. In conclusion, our data support the development of the MYC/GSPT1 degrader GT19630 as a therapeutic strategy for MYC-driven hematologic malignancies.

papers.abstract: Abstract Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN) is an orphan, aggressive hematologic malignancy characterized by high CD123 expression. Tagraxofusp (TAG), a CD123-directed toxin, is the first approved therapy. Prior studies demonstrated BPDCN dependence on BCL2, sensitivity to venetoclax (VEN), and reversal of TAG resistance with azacitidine (AZA). We conducted a phase 2 study evaluating combination therapy with TAG, AZA, and VEN in patients with BPDCN. Patients with previously untreated (1L) or relapsed/refractory (R/R) BPDCN received 28-day cycles of AZA (75 mg/m2 on days 1-7), VEN (400 mg on days 1-21), and TAG (12 μg/kg on days 4-6). Eligibility followed TAG guidelines to mitigate risk of capillary leak syndrome (CLS). Twenty-seven patients were enrolled (16 1L, 11 R/R), with median age of 70 years (range, 21-81). Composite complete remission (composed of: complete remission [CR], CR with incomplete count recovery, and CR clinical) rates were 88% in 1L and 64% in R/R cohorts. Median duration of response was not reached in 1L and was 7.2 months in R/R patients. CLS occurred in 15% of patients, most were grade 2. In the 1L cohort, median overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were not reached; the 2-year OS was 65% and 2-year PFS was 53%. Median OS in R/R patients was 8.4 months. A high proportion of patients proceeded to allogeneic stem cell transplantation in remission (63% in 1L, including 10/11 patients aged ≤75 years; 55% in R/R). TAG-AZA-VEN is highly active in both 1L and relapsed BPDCN with a predictable and manageable safety profile, supporting its use as a new therapeutic option. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as #NCT03113643.

papers.abstract: Abstract Immunotherapy has revolutionized the treatment of solid cancers in recent years. However, T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas (T-NHL) originate from immune cells themselves and are biologically heterogeneous, rendering investigations of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) mechanisms of action complex. Although case reports and individual anaplastic large cell lymphoma (ALCL) patients enrolled in T-NHL trials demonstrated favorable responses to ICIs, hyperprogression was observed in other T-NHL subtypes. We therefore used a syngeneic mouse model of anaplastic lymphoma kinase positive (ALK+) ALCL to investigate immune surveillance and ICI-induced immune response. Transplantation experiments combined with the depletion of relevant immune axes revealed that ALCL immune surveillance is mediated by CD4+ T cells and natural killer cells. Innate and adaptive immune cell infiltration was confirmed in a large series of primary human ALK+ ALCL samples. ICI monotherapy demonstrated robust efficacy in murine ALCL, inducing complete remissions in ∼50% of treated animals. Mechanistically, PD-L1 blockade reversed regulatory T cell-mediated immunosuppression and increased the frequency of circulating effector CD8+ T lymphocytes, thereby significantly prolonging survival. Importantly, CD4+ T cells proved indispensable for driving and sustaining immunotherapy-induced antitumor responses in murine ALCL. CD4+ T cells of nonresponder animals exhibited an exhausted phenotype and a transcriptomic T helper 22–like signature, implicating persistent T-cell exhaustion and polarization as a meaningful immune evasion mechanism. Our findings uncover CD4+ T cells as key players in spontaneous and immunotherapy-mediated anti–T-cell lymphoma immunity, which demonstrates the critically needed preclinical proof-of-concept for the safe and effective use of immunotherapy for ALCL.

papers.abstract: Abstract Patients with acute leukemias harboring translocations involving gene lysine methyltransferase 2A (KMT2A) have a poor prognosis due to chemotherapy resistance with rapid relapse following standard treatments. The resulting KMT2A fusion proteins dysregulate gene expression, leading to an upregulation of leukemogenic transcription factors such as HOXA9 and MEIS1, which drives leukemic transformation. Although menin inhibitors are proving to be promising new therapeutics for patients with KMT2A-rearranged (KMT2Ar) acute leukemia, resistance mechanisms have already been described and new therapeutic approaches for this patient subgroup must be identified. Here, a genome-wide CRISPR/Cas9 screen in a KMT2Ar B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia cell line identified the deubiquitinase ubiquitin-specific peptidase 22 (USP22) as a novel regulator of MEIS1 protein stability. USP22 is a member of the Spt-Ada-Gcn5 acetyltransferase multiprotein complex, which has crucial functions in shaping the chromatin landscape and modulating transcription. Genetic depletion of USP22 impaired cellular growth and proliferation in KMT2Ar acute leukemia models. Chromatin immunoprecipitation revealed cooperative binding between USP22 and MEIS1 at critical oncogenic target genes, suggesting that USP22 safeguards leukemogenic transcription by protecting MEIS1 from proteasomal degradation. Genetic or chemical inhibition of USP22 led to the polyubiquitination of MEIS1, resulting in proteasomal degradation and downregulation of the expression of target genes. Our study identifies USP22 as a novel regulator of MEIS1 protein stability that could potentially be exploited as a therapeutic target in the future in KMT2Ar leukemias.

papers.abstract: Abstract To date, non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide, underscoring the urgent need for new treatment options. The oncofetal carbohydrate CD176 is masked on healthy tissues but is present on a variety of cancer entities and is associated with cancer invasiveness and metastasis. In this study, we employed chimeric antigen receptor T cells (CAR-T) directed against CD176 for treatment of NSCLC. CD176-CAR-Ts were optimized with an additional inducible cassette encoding IL18 (CD176-iIL18-TRUCK) or IL12 (CD176-iIL12-TRUCK) to augment antitumor reactivity through autocrine and paracrine signaling. CD176-iIL18- and CD176-iIL12-TRUCKs eradicated NSCLC cells in a three-dimensional tumor spheroid model and tissue slices derived from patients with lung adenocarcinoma more potently than CD176-CAR-Ts. Administration of TRUCKs in a lung carcinoma xenograft mouse model resulted in partial or complete tumor eradication in all mice treated with CD176-iIL12-TRUCKs and in 50% of mice treated with CD176-iIL18-TRUCKs. This study highlights the potential of CD176 as a CAR T-cell target and suggests CD176-CAR-Ts armored with IL18 or IL12 as a promising new therapeutic approach for the treatment of NSCLC and several other CD176-positive cancer entities.

papers.abstract: Background: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) are common toxicities of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but their prognostic implications in older adults remain uncertain. Patients and Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using SEER–Medicare (2010–2019). We included patients aged ≥66 years with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC who initiated ICI monotherapy or chemoimmunotherapy from 2015–2017. Follow-up began at treatment initiation and continued until death, Medicare disenrollment, or December 31, 2019. The primary exposure was a clinically meaningful irAE, defined as an irAE diagnosis with evidence of systemic immunosuppressant use and/or treatment delay, or discontinuation. In secondary analyses, we categorized patients as having no irAE, an irAE managed without hospitalization, or an irAE requiring hospitalization. The primary outcome was overall survival. We estimated adjusted survival differences and restricted mean survival time using doubly robust causal inference methods. Results: The cohort included 5,304 patients (mean age, 75 years; 52.7% female; 81.9% White). Clinically meaningful irAEs occurred in 1,807 (34.1%) patients, with a median onset of 3.8 months (IQR, 1.1–9.4). Death occurred in 65.1% of patients with irAEs and 78.7% without irAEs, corresponding to an adjusted absolute survival benefit of 6.6% (95% CI, 5.3%–8.0%) and a 6.5-month gain in restricted mean survival time (95% CI, 5.6–7.4). In secondary analyses, irAEs managed without hospitalization showed the greatest benefit (odds ratio [OR], 0.44; 95% CI, 0.35–0.54), whereas irAE hospitalization was associated with attenuated benefit (OR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89–0.99). Conclusions: Among older adults with advanced NSCLC receiving ICIs, clinically meaningful irAEs were associated with improved overall survival, particularly when managed without hospitalization. These findings highlight the clinical importance of early recognition of immune-related toxicities; irAE-related hospitalization may identify a higher-risk group warranting closer monitoring and supportive care.

papers.abstract: Abstract Cancer immunotherapies have achieved meaningful clinical benefits but remain limited by systemic toxicities that restrict the use of potent immune modulators. CD47-targeting antibodies promote tumor cell phagocytosis but are hindered by hematologic toxicity, whereas IL2 activates cytotoxic lymphocytes but induces broad, dose-limiting immune activation. In this study, we engineered a reciprocally masked antibody–cytokine fusion [CD47-specific antibody (aCD47)/IL2/IL2 receptor complex (IL2c)] designed for tumor-selective activation. In this construct, an aCD47 and an IL2c sterically and functionally suppress each other via protease-cleavable linkers, preventing CD47 blockade and IL2 receptor engagement in circulation while enabling protease-dependent unmasking within the tumor microenvironment. A human construct demonstrated masking and protease-dependent restoration of both CD47–signal regulatory protein alpha (SIRPα) blockade and IL2 signaling, with improved systemic tolerability in human CD47/SIRPα transgenic mice, supporting translational potential. A murine analog enabled mechanistic and efficacy studies in immunocompetent tumor models. The tolerability of mouse aCD47/IL2c was improved in comparison with individual components. Antitumor activity required both CD47 blockade and IL2 activity and resulted in robust antitumor efficacy, including in an immune checkpoint–resistant melanoma model. The robust antitumor efficacy was associated with inflammatory macrophage polarization and increased numbers of effector CD8+ T cells inside the tumor. Unlike conventional CD47 antibodies or IL2 therapies, this approach enabled coordinated, tumor-localized activation of innate and adaptive immunity while limiting systemic exposure. Together, these data highlight reciprocal masking as a clinically relevant strategy to expand the therapeutic index of immune modulators constrained by systemic toxicity.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Relapse occurs in 10%–20% of children with hepatoblastoma and is associated with inferior outcomes, yet standardized management remains limited. Defining risk factors and relapse patterns, as well as the role of surgery, particularly transplantation, is critical to optimizing survival. A retrospective review was performed of patients aged 0–18 years diagnosed with hepatoblastoma from 2007 to 2024. Demographics, tumor characteristics, treatment course, relapse patterns, and outcomes were collected. Analyses included univariable and multivariable logistic regression, Kaplan–Meier survival estimation, and log‐rank testing. Among 135 patients, 98 (72.6%) achieved remission without relapse, 32 (23.7%) relapsed, and 5 (3.7%) experienced primary progression without remission. Older age, PRETEXT (pretreatment extent of disease) IV, metastatic disease at diagnosis, and macrovascular invasion were associated with relapse on univariable analysis, but only older age remained independently associated with relapse (adjusted odds ratio 1.27 per year, 95% confidence interval 1.05–1.53); PRETEXT IV and metastatic disease were not significantly associated with overall survival. Lung‐only relapse demonstrated favorable survival (100% alive), whereas combined liver and lung or extrahepatic relapse had poorer outcomes (40%–44% alive), although survival did not differ significantly across relapse sites ( p = 0.15). Of 54 liver transplant recipients, 44 underwent upfront transplantation, and 10 underwent salvage transplantation, with no significant difference in overall survival ( p = 0.90), although the salvage group was small. Relapse or progression after upfront transplantation occurred in 27% of recipients; lung‐only relapse again conferred favorable survival. Long‐term survival is achievable in relapsed hepatoblastoma, particularly for isolated pulmonary relapse. Older age, likely a surrogate for adverse tumor biology, was associated with relapse but did not preclude survival when aggressive multimodal therapy was used. Salvage transplantation achieved durable survival in selected patients and should be considered for unresectable intrahepatic relapse when extrahepatic disease is absent or controlled.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Phosphatidylinositol 3‐kinase catalytic subunit type 3 (PIK3C3) is central to autophagy, which supports cancer adaptation to environmental stresses and may contribute to drug resistance. KRAS ‐mutant cancers have been reported to require autophagy for survival. We investigated the influence of KRAS mutation status on the roles of PIK3C3 in colorectal cancer (CRC) cell viability and chemosensitivity in vitro, as well as its association with patient prognosis. Methods The clinical significance of PIK3C3 expression in relation to KRAS mutation status was evaluated by immunohistochemistry in patients with advanced CRC. Cell viability, colony formation, and spheroid formation assays were performed using CRC cell lines. Results In KRAS ‐wild‐type ( KRAS ‐WT) Caco‐2 and Colo320 cells, PIK3C3 and the KRAS/ERK pathway appeared to positively regulate each other. In contrast, PIK3C3 inhibition did not reduce p‐ERK levels or induce significant p62 accumulation in KRAS ‐mutant SW480 and HCT116 cells. PIK3C3 knockdown reduced cell viability but increased resistance to 5‐fluorouracil (5‐FU) in Caco‐2 and Colo320 cells, whereas the opposite effect was observed in SW480 and HCT116 cells. Transfection with a KRAS ‐mutant plasmid sensitized Caco‐2 cells to 5‐FU accompanied by reduced thymidylate synthase (TS) and β‐catenin levels following PIK3C3 inhibition. Clinically, high PIK3C3 expression was associated with KRAS mutation and poorer survival in patients with advanced CRC. Its adverse short‐term prognostic association was more pronounced in KRAS ‐mutant CRC than in KRAS ‐WT CRC. Conclusion Based on preclinical in vitro findings, PIK3C3 appears to support KRAS ‐WT and KRAS ‐mutant CRCs in different ways. Notably, PIK3C3 inhibition enhances 5‐FU sensitivity in KRAS ‐mutant CRC cells, potentially through TS regulation, and warrants further investigation as a therapeutic strategy.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Cancer incidence in Africa is projected to reach 2.1 million new cases annually by 2040. Current treatment guidelines remain largely based on pharmacogenomic data predominantly from European and Asian genetic profiles, potentially compromising safety and efficacy in African patients. However, limited clinical validation data, extreme intra‐population genetic diversity, and significant healthcare infrastructure barriers constrain the translational application of pharmacogenomics in Africa. Objective This review critically examines pharmacogenomic variants with established clinical actionability in cancer treatment, focusing on those with differential frequencies or African‐specific alleles, and evaluates the evidence base for their implementation in African healthcare settings. Methods We searched PubMed/MEDLINE, PharmGKB, dbSNP, and Google Scholar for peer‐reviewed studies reporting pharmacogenomic variants in African or African‐ancestry populations relevant to cancer therapeutics. We synthesised evidence from recent African and global studies on pharmacogenomic variants affecting commonly used chemotherapy agents. Results Several variants show marked frequency differences between African‐ancestry reference populations and European populations, including DPYD rs115232898 (2.06% vs. 0.00%), CYP2D6 * 17 ( 18.76% vs. 0% ), and CYP3A5 *6 (12.82% vs. 0%). However, many of these estimates derive primarily from African‐American datasets and should not be interpreted as representative of continental African populations. African‐specific variants such as CYP2D6 * 17 and DPYD rs115232898 are underrepresented in guideline development datasets. Intra‐African genetic diversity is the highest globally, with Khoi‐San populations harbouring extensive private variation, suggesting that no single pharmacogenomic panel will be universally applicable across the continent. Conclusion While pharmacogenomics holds substantial promise for personalising cancer treatment in Africa, its current translational readiness is limited by a critical lack of African‐specific clinical validation data. Priorities include multi‐site validation studies, development of African‐enriched genotyping panels, and integration of pharmacogenomic education into oncology practice. Implementation must be accompanied by ethical frameworks ensuring data sovereignty and equitable benefit‐sharing.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Polygenic risk scores (PRS) and lifestyle factors are associated with colorectal cancer (CRC), but whether their associations and joint effects vary according to age at CRC onset remains unclear. We evaluated age‐related heterogeneity in the associations of genetic risk and lifestyle with CRC and examined their additive interaction in early‐ and late‐onset CRC. Methods We analyzed data from 405,453 cancer‐free participants aged 38–73 years at baseline in the UK Biobank. PRS and a healthy lifestyle score (based on eight modifiable factors) were assessed. Age‐scale Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for CRC risk by age at onset. Heterogeneity across age intervals was assessed using likelihood ratio tests. Additive interaction was assessed using the relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI), and differences in standardized incidence rates were evaluated. Results During a median follow‐up of 13.65 years, 6620 CRC cases were identified. Compared with low genetic risk, high genetic risk was associated with HRs of 3.72, 3.32, 2.80, and 2.01 for CRC occurring at ages < 55, 55–64, 65–74, and ≥ 75 years, respectively, with significant heterogeneity across age intervals ( p for heterogeneity < 0.001). Compared with a favorable lifestyle, the corresponding HRs for an unfavorable lifestyle were 1.10, 1.50, 1.58, and 1.28, respectively, with evidence of overall heterogeneity ( p for heterogeneity = 0.015). For late‐onset CRC, positive additive interactions were observed for an unfavorable lifestyle combined with intermediate or high genetic risk, whereas no such interaction was detected for early‐onset CRC. Conclusions The associations of genetic susceptibility and baseline lifestyle with CRC varied according to age at onset. Positive additive interaction between genetic risk and an unfavorable lifestyle was observed for late‐onset but not early‐onset CRC. These findings provide further evidence that the relative and joint associations of genetic and lifestyle factors with CRC vary across the life course.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background The Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (OMOP CDM) is a data standard that enables multicenter research. Primary objective was to describe the magnitude of healthcare utilization in pediatric cancer versus non‐cancer patients. Secondary objective was to compare 6‐month clinical outcomes related to abnormal lab tests and mortality. Methods In this multicenter retrospective study, we included pediatric patients 0–18 years at first medication administration. Cancer patients had a malignant neoplastic disease diagnosis and received chemotherapy. Index date was the first chemotherapy date. Non‐cancer patients were assigned analogous index dates based on randomly sampled first medication to chemotherapy intervals. Outcomes were measured within 6 months of index date. Healthcare utilization included encounters, procedures, radiology, lab tests, and medications. Results Among 2810 cancer and 11,240 non‐cancer patients, all evaluated healthcare utilization measures were significantly more common in cancer patients. The largest relative differences were observed for long inpatient stay (risk ratio [RR] 26.32, 95% confidence interval [CI] 15.00–46.17), computed tomography (RR 23.59, 95% CI 19.24–28.92), blood culture (RR 37.04, 95% CI 9.58–143.14), and intravenous medication (RR 17.69, 95% CI 8.75–35.75). Death within 6 months was higher for cancer versus non‐cancer patients (RR 38.37, 95% CI 12.91–114.04). Conclusions Using the OMOP CDM, we found greater healthcare utilization and worse clinical outcomes among pediatric cancer patients than non‐cancer patients, with the largest relative differences observed for inpatient stay, computed tomography, blood culture, and intravenous medication. These findings provide insight into resource utilization patterns and illustrate the OMOP CDM research potential for multicenter studies.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Metastasis of malignant tumors arising from epithelial organs to sentinel lymph nodes has important implications for prognosis, staging, and therapeutic decision‐making. Recent insights into anatomic pathways, pathogenesis, molecular interactions, and genetic factors have encouraged scientists and clinicians to develop drugs that target mechanisms of lymph node metastasis. We summarize important aspects of the vast literature that pertains to these mechanisms, focusing on five phases that implicate invasion through the epithelial basement membrane and tumor microenvironment, into initial lymphatics, and, after flow through lymphatic trunks, into the sentinel lymph node. Valuable information regarding tumor cell‐directed motility, lymphangiogenesis, host cells that enhance metastasis, immune responses to tumor antigens, and tumor‐induced changes in sentinel lymph node(s) provides a promising avenue for the continued development of new therapeutic approaches to prevent and treat metastasis. This article reviews these aspects by synthesizing current scientific and clinical advances and translating them for medical professionals.

papers.abstract: To evaluate the prospective risk of high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion or worse (HSIL+) in high-risk HPV (HR-HPV)positive women, assessing the independent and interactive effects of baseline HPV16-status, genotype multiplicity, and follow-up HPV persistence. A prospective cohort of 2562 HR-HPV-positive women referred for colposcopy were categorized into four groups: single non-HPV16, single HPV16, HPV16 plus other HR types, or multiple non-HPV16. HSIL+ risk was analysed using Cox-proportional-hazards-regression, restricted mean survival time (RMST) at 36months, and Fine-Gray competing-risk models. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated concurrent HSIL+ risk associated with follow-up HPV persistence. Overall, 691 women (27.0%) developed HSIL+. Infection with HPV16 plus other HR types carried the highest risk (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR]2.10, 95%CI: 1.69-2.62) and shorter median HSIL+-free survival than single non-HPV16 infection (24 vs. 54months), corresponding to 5.1 fewer HSIL+-free-months at 36months (p<0.001). Baseline HPV16 positivity and genotype multiplicity exerted independent, additive effects without multiplicative interaction (adjusted p=0.600). Incorporating multiplicity improved model discrimination beyond entry cytology and HPV16 status (concordance index 0.612 vs. 0.587, p<0.001). Results remained robust in competing-risk analyses (subdistribution HR2.03, 95%CI: 1.64-2.52) and after excluding early-treated women (aHR2.00, 95%CI: 1.52-2.62). Follow-up viral persistence strongly correlated with concurrent HSIL+ (aHR5.71-8.59, p<0.001), reflecting a cross-sectional risk correlation complementary to baseline prognostication. Baseline HPV16 positivity and genotype multiplicity are independent, additive risk factors for HSIL+, with HPV16 plus other HR types marking the highest-risk subgroup. Genotype multiplicity provides distinct clinical predictive value alongside HPV16 status, while follow-up HPV persistence offers complementary, non-redundant information for concurrent risk evaluation in risk-based management strategies.

papers.abstract: The IL-36γ/IL-36R signaling axis mediates cellular communication in various contexts and has recently been implicated in pro-fibrotic responses. However, its specific role in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), which is characterized by abundant cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), remains elusive. Here, we investigated the contribution of IL-36γ/IL-36R signaling to CAF function and OSCC progression. Immunohistochemical analysis of patient samples revealed that IL-36γ was highly expressed in CAFs and that higher co-expression of IL-36γ/IL-36R in CAFs was associated with more invasive patterns and shorter disease-free survival. By integrating tumor cell lines with patient-derived organoids (PDOs), we established three co-culture systems to model these interactions. These models revealed that IL-36γ signaling enhanced CAF proliferation and extracellular matrix remodeling. Mechanistically, the IL-36γ/IL-36R axis in CAFs increased ERK1/2-dependent CCL20 secretion, which in turn promoted tumor cell invasion. Pharmacological blockade of IL-36R attenuated both the IL-36γ-induced increase in CAF abundance and the associated pro-tumorigenic CAF phenotypes in vivo. Collectively, these findings suggest that the IL-36γ/IL-36R-ERK1/2-CCL20 signaling cascade participates in CAF-tumor interactions. Targeting IL-36R may therefore represent a promising therapeutic strategy for invasive OSCC.

papers.abstract: Analysis of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) methylation can enable noninvasive disease detection by leveraging tissue-specific epigenetic differences between malignant and nonmalignant cells. However, such analyses can be confounded by the repair of jagged DNA fragment ends during double-stranded sequencing library preparation, which introduces spurious methylation signals into cfDNA molecules. Here we present JEEPERS, a framework to detect and correct jagged-end-induced methylation errors while preserving duplex integrity and native methylation patterns. We showed high fidelity for measuring tumor burden and demonstrated allele-specific methylation differences at recurrent somatic mutations, revealing a link between adjacent CpG methylation and EGFR/TP53 driver and resistance mutations. We further demonstrated enhanced diagnostic performance across liquid biopsy applications, including tumor-type-specific methylation profiles, hemimethylation profiling, epigenetic-clock-based age estimation and cell type deconvolution. By faithfully correcting end-repair errors, JEEPERS provides a versatile framework for integrating mutations and methylation features in cfDNA at high resolution, enabling more precise molecular profiling and disease monitoring.

papers.abstract: To elucidate the mechanisms underlying therapy-induced resistance, we investigated the temporal dynamics of the polyploid giant cancer cell (PGCC) life cycle following treatment with the microtubule-destabilizing agent vincristine (VCR). Longitudinal live-cell fluorescence imaging revealed that VCR-induced mitotic suppression activated a distinct PGCC life cycle characterized by nuclear amplification and progressive cellular reprogramming. At the cellular level, PGCCs entered a senescence-like state accompanied by an enhanced senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), increased epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), acquisition of early embryonic-like features, and multilineage differentiation potential into ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm. PGCC-derived progeny exhibited dose- and time-dependent changes in proliferative behavior, aggressive phenotypes in vitro, along with time-dependent tumorigenic potential in vivo. Remarkably, at the tissue level, PGCCs also underwent spatial nuclear reorganization and self-organization into morphologically defined glandular epithelial structures exhibiting varying degrees of tissue maturation, reminiscent of early embryonic development. Silencing IL1β, IL6, or IL8, or pharmacologically inhibiting their receptors, suppressed PGCC formation, budding, EMT, and embryonic-like reprogramming associated with tissue morphogenesis. Furthermore, NAMPT emerged as a key regulator of embryonic-like stemness, glandular morphogenesis, and structural expansion. Together, these findings reveal that therapeutic stress activates a PGCC life cycle capable of generating two divergent outcomes: resistant tumor regeneration through clonal selection of undifferentiated tumor cells and organized tissue differentiation through spatial nuclear reprogramming. Our study establishes a conceptual framework linking therapy-induced polyploidization, developmental plasticity, and resistance generation at both cellular and tissue levels.

papers.abstract: KRASG12D is a predominant driver in pancreatic cancer, yet the basis of intrinsic resistance to KRASG12D-targeted therapy remains poorly defined. Integrated genomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics profiling across 242 patient-derived organoids (PDOs) and matched tumor tissues reveals a KRASG12D-mutant subset intrinsically resistant to KRASG12D-targeted therapeutics, characterized by marked downregulation of innate immune signaling pathways. Functional validation demonstrates that suppressing interferon signaling in sensitive models induces resistance, whereas activation of interferon signaling, particularly interferon beta (IFN-β), increases sensitivity in resistant models. Combining IFN-β with KRAS inhibitors (MRTX1133, HRS-4642, and RMC-6236) exhibits synergistic antitumor effects in intrinsically resistant pancreatic cancer. Mechanistically, sustained MYC activity is associated with attenuated sensitivity to KRAS inhibition and correlates with repressed interferon signaling, suggesting a potential role in promoting intrinsic resistance. These findings identify interferon signaling as a candidate determinant of KRAS-targeted therapy response and support interferon-based combinations as a potential strategy for intrinsically resistant pancreatic cancer.

papers.abstract: Despite their considerable promise, many current medical foundation models remain modality specific and lack transparent reasoning, limiting clinical adoption. To address this gap, we introduce Explainable Vision Language Foundation Model for Medicine (EVLF-FM), a multimodal vision language foundation model that combines broad diagnostic capabilities with fine-grained explainability. The development and testing of EVLF-FM encompassed more than 1.3 million total samples from 18 global datasets across 10 imaging modalities related to six clinical specialties: dermatology, hepatology, ophthalmology, pathology, pulmonology and radiology. External validation employed 13,443 independent test samples from 17 additional datasets across 10 imaging modalities. EVLF-FM supports disease diagnosis, visual question answering and pixel-level visual grounding with reasoning capabilities. In internal validation for disease diagnostics, EVLF-FM achieved the highest average accuracy, 0.895, outperforming leading generalist and specialist models. In medical visual grounding, EVLF-FM also achieved reasonable performance across nine modalities with average accuracy at 0.5 intersection over union (Acc@0.5) of 0.842. External testing further confirmed consistent zero-shot and few-shot performance, with competitive F1 scores despite a smaller model size. A hybrid training strategy combining supervised and visual reinforcement fine-tuning enables EVLF-FM to generate clinically interpretable explanations aligned with visual evidence. Human evaluation of these reasoning outputs using the S.C.O.R.E. framework yielded a high overall mean score of 4.25/5, supporting their clinical interpretability. Current limitations include the need for additional validation across diverse healthcare settings. Prospective clinical studies are required to evaluate the safety, effectiveness and clinical utility of EVLF-FM before routine clinical deployment.

papers.abstract: The clinical adoption of deep learning in pathology is largely hindered by the "black box" nature of current models, which often obscure the biological basis of prognosis. Here, we introduce MorphX, an interpretable framework that predicts patient survival by explicitly decoding multi-scale morphological patterns from whole-slide images. Unlike conventional methods relying on latent features, MorphX fuses macro-scale tissue texture with micro-scale nuclear metrics to attribute risk to interpretable biological phenotypes. In a multi-center study spanning 1,067 patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), MorphX achieves concordance indices of 0.775-0.799 in discovery cohorts. Crucially, we derive eight distinct morphology-based biomarkers-driven by texture heterogeneity in necrotic regions, lymphocyte density, and nuclear shape-that demonstrate reproducible survival associations across independent cohorts, offering a granular resolution of tumor aggressiveness that transcends traditional histological grading. By translating opaque computational predictions into validated biological insights, MorphX supports trustworthy, transparent, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven precision oncology.

papers.abstract: Sex differences in glioblastoma (GBM) outcomes are shaped by biological, hormonal, and immune factors, but the mechanisms driving these disparities remain unclear. We identify platelet protease-activated receptor 4 (PAR4) signaling as a regulator of sex-specific anti-tumor immunity. GBM patients exhibit increased platelet reactivity driven by PAR4. In murine models, pharmacologic or genetic inhibition of PAR4 prolongs survival in females, but not males, and is estrogen dependent, persisting in hormonal females regardless of chromosomal sex. The survival advantage is mediated within the tumor microenvironment through enhanced CD8+ T cell infiltration and function. PAR4-activated platelets suppress CD8+ T cell activity, whereas CD8+ T cell depletion abolishes both tumor-induced platelet reactivity and the PAR4-dependent survival advantage. Mechanistically, PAR4 inhibition enhances CD8+ T cell signaling through interaction with estrogen receptor β (ERβ). These findings demonstrate that platelets are critical regulators of sex-specific anti-tumor immunity and identify PAR4 as a promising therapeutic target in cancer.

papers.abstract: The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EO-CRC; diagnosed before age 50 years) is increasing worldwide. Although current data indicate that EO-CRC may be biologically distinct from average-onset CRC (AO-CRC; diagnosed at age ≥50 years), molecular differences remain poorly defined. To address this knowledge gap, we generated a single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) atlas from 189 primary CRC tumors (54 EO-CRC, 135 AO-CRC) spanning eight decades of life, with at least 20 tumors in most age decades. Our analyses stratified tumors by microsatellite status and accounted for tumor sidedness, stage, patient sex and neoadjuvant treatment history, modeling age continuously or categorically (EO-CRC versus AO-CRC). Among microsatellite-stable (MSS) tumors, those from younger patients were characterized by increased stromal and decreased epithelial proportions, which we confirmed using multispectral immunofluorescence and machine learning in an external cohort of 712 MSS CRC tumors (18 EO-CRC, 694 AO-CRC). Tumor epithelial cells from young patients exhibited increased expression of long noncoding RNAs and FN1, with a trend toward increased heterogeneity in copy number alterations. MSS left-sided EO-CRC tumors had more cell-cell interactions, with epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition-related signaling pathways (FN1/GDF/ACTIVIN) showing increased, cell type-specific interactions. Our large high-resolution snRNA-seq atlas uncovers age-associated features of CRC and provides a resource for the community to understand EO-CRC biology.

papers.abstract: PHERGain was a randomized, non-comparative phase 2 trial evaluating a positron 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography (18F-FDG-PET)-guided, pathological complete response (pCR)-adapted strategy to omit chemotherapy in HER2-positive early breast cancer. Female patients with HER2-positive stages I-IIIA operable breast cancer (tumor size ≥ 1.5 cm) were randomized to receive chemotherapy plus trastuzumab and pertuzumab (HP; group A) or HP ± endocrine therapy (group B). In group B, treatment was adapted according to 18F-FDG-PET response after two cycles and pCR, with chemotherapy administered to nonresponders or patients without pCR. We previously reported that this de-escalation approach revealed a 3-year invasive disease-free survival (iDFS) of 94.3% (95% confidence interval (CI): 90.9 to 96.8) in group B. Here we report the prespecified secondary endpoint, 5-year iDFS and exploratory circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) findings. After a median follow-up of 5.6 years, the 5-year iDFS was 89.5% (95% CI: 85.7 to 93.4) in group B (n = 267) and 92.4% (95% CI: 86.7 to 98.5) among 18F-FDG-PET responders achieving pCR without chemotherapy (n = 86), with one distant recurrence. The latter estimate describes a long-term outcome in a post-randomization subgroup defined by 18F-FDG-PET response and pCR and should be interpreted as descriptive rather than as causal effects of omitting chemotherapy. Detectable ctDNA at baseline or during treatment was associated with inferior iDFS, whereas ctDNA clearance correlated with higher pCR rates and improved long-term outcomes. These findings continue to support the clinical validity of an 18F-FDG-PET-guided, pCR-adapted approach and suggest a potential role for ctDNA in refining treatment individualization. papers.abstract: Abstract Despite decades of investigation, the fundamental molecular and cellular principles that enable bacteria to thrive within the tumor microenvironment have yet to be defined. Here, through a genome‑wide functional screen, we identify the bacterial genes and pathways that govern intratumoral fitness. Targeted deletion of nonglucose phosphotransferase systems to align bacterial metabolic preference with tumor metabolite availability promotes bacterial intratumoral fitness. Integrating multiple metabolic adaptations into a single tumor‑avid Escherichia coli strain (Ec‑TA) results in increased tumor colonization, not only after intratumoral delivery but also after intravenous delivery, leading to increased anti‑tumor efficacy when using Ec‑TA engineered to deliver an encoded immunostimulatory payload. Furthermore, Ec‑TA displaces wild‑type bacteria from pre‑colonized tumors when administered systemically, underscoring its potential for locally delivering therapeutics in the presence of resident tumor microbes. These data demonstrate that adapting bacteria to the unique characteristics of the tumor metabolic microenvironment can drive the development of safer and more effective chassis for next‑generation bacterial cancer therapies.

papers.abstract: Abstract Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) affect up to 40% of patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors, yet identification requires laborious, inconsistent manual chart review. Here we show that agentic artificial intelligence coupled with human verification could enhance efficiency, performance and consistency for irAE assessment. We developed and evaluated an agentic large language model system to extract the presence, temporality, severity grade, attribution and certainty of six irAE types from clinical notes. Retrospectively, the system achieved a macro-averaged F 1 of 0.92 for current-event detection and 0.66 for multi-class severity grading; self-consistency improved F 1 by 0.14. The best-performing configuration cost approximately US$0.02 per note. In prospective silent deployment over 3 months, the binary F 1 was 0.72–0.79. In a randomized crossover study of clinical trial staff, agentic assistance reduced annotation time by 2.71 min ( P < 0.001), increased complete-match accuracy (odds ratio 1.45; 95% confidence interval 1.01–2.08; P = 0.045) and improved interannotator agreement (Krippendorff’s α from 0.22–0.51 to 0.82–0.85).

papers.abstract: Dysnatremia is common in critically ill patients and has been linked to poor outcomes and renal prognosis. Burn patients are particularly vulnerable, but the prognostic significance of dysnatremia in this population remains unclear. We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of 1,758 burn patients admitted to a French burn center between 2011 and 2023. Dysnatremia was defined as at least one episode of hyponatremia ( 145 mmol/L) during intensive care unit (ICU) stay. The primary endpoint was the incidence of dysnatremia; secondary endpoints included major adverse kidney events (MAKE) at ICU discharge and acute kidney injury (AKI) occurrence and severity. Dysnatremia occurred in 56.3% of patients (n = 990), with hyponatremia in 50.5% (n = 888) and hypernatremia in 23.8% (n = 418). MAKE at ICU discharge did not differ between hyponatremic and normonatremic patients (12.6% vs. 10.9%, p = 0.304) but was sixfold higher with hypernatremia (32.3% vs. 5.4%, p < 0.001). After adjustment for age and burned total body surface area, hypernatremia was independently associated with MAKE at ICU discharge (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 4.03; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.92-5.56; p < 0.001), whereas hyponatremia was not (aHR 1.15; 95% CI: 0.85-1.55; p = 0.377). Clustering analysis identified three phenotypes: Cluster B (severe burns, worst outcomes), Cluster A (older patients, mostly hyponatremic, intermediate outcomes), and Cluster C (younger patients, mild burns, best outcomes). Dysnatremia affects over half of burn patients. Sodium disturbances should be viewed as markers of systemic severity, warranting close monitoring and preventive strategies.

papers.abstract: Fluid accumulation in surgical patients is associated with worse outcomes. Lung ultrasound (LUS) and venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) grading can assess congestion and thereby fluid tolerance. However, evidence regarding epidemiology, feasibility, and associations of reduced fluid tolerance with outcomes in surgical patients is lacking. This was a prospective single-centre observational cohort study in patients undergoing major gastrointestinal surgery. LUS and VExUS were performed before surgery and daily for up to 5 days after surgery. Reduced fluid tolerance was defined as pulmonary congestion (B profile on LUS), systemic congestion (VExUS ≥2), or both. The primary outcome was the prevalence of reduced fluid tolerance. Secondary outcomes were feasibility of ultrasound assessments, Clavien-Dindo grade ≥3 complications, and length of stay (LOS). Of the 200 participants included, 73 (37%) exhibited signs of reduced fluid tolerance, most commonly on postoperative day 4 (n=28; 14%). Reduced fluid tolerance was primarily driven by pulmonary congestion (n=69; 95%), whereas systemic congestion was rare. In most affected patients (47 of 73; 64%), reduced fluid tolerance was limited to 1 day. Of 1200 planned assessments, 146 (12%) were missing: 123 because participants declined, mostly owing to the burden of repeated assessments, and 23 (2%) because of incomplete views. Reduced fluid tolerance was associated with LOS of >7 days (odds ratio 3.29; 95% CI 1.03-10.70), but not with major postoperative complications (hazard ratio 1.18; 95% CI 0.49-2.86). Reduced fluid tolerance detected by ultrasound is common after major gastrointestinal surgery and associated with increased LOS. Ultrasound assessments were technically feasible, but repeated assessments were perceived as a burden by a substantial proportion of patients. NCT06166719 (principal investigator: A.P.J. Vlaar; first registered: 04-12-2023).

papers.abstract: Cells resist viral infection by triggering rapid and sensitive innate immune responses, initiated by cytoplasmic viral sensor proteins (CyVSP), retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I), melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA-5), and protein kinase R (PKR). Our single-cell analysis reveals that viral replication requires a supra-unitary viral genome input, significantly more than one, which we define as the virion input threshold for replication (VITREP). This threshold varies depending on viruses and cell types, independently of viral protein synthesis. Through mathematical modeling and experimental testing, we uncover that supra-unitary viral genome quantities activate negative feedback regulators (NFR) of CyVSP, including death-associated protein kinase 1 (DAPK1), Rio kinase 3 (RIOK3), and protein phosphatase 2 regulatory subunit alpha (PPP2R2A), that suppress innate immune responses and allow replication. We validate key predictions of our model, namely that downregulating NFR reduces replication, whereas upregulating NFR or coinfecting cells promotes replication. Together, these findings reveal a fundamental mechanism governing viral infectivity and tissue tropism.

papers.abstract: To determine whether injection pressure and pressure-time characteristics can discriminate potentially hazardous needle-tip locations during peripheral nerve injection. Systematic review of experimental preclinical studies with narrative synthesis. Animal, ex vivo biological nerve, and human cadaver models of peripheral nerve injection. Needle placement and injection at intraneural, intrafascicular, perineural, or extraneural locations. CENTRAL, PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to April 28, 2026 and updated on September 19, 2026. Studies reporting opening, peak, or plateau pressure or pressure-time characteristics in relation to anatomically defined needle-tip location were eligible. Human clinical studies and non-biological bench models were excluded. Risk of bias was evaluated using SYRCLE for animal studies and a domain-based framework for cadaveric studies. Because of substantial heterogeneity in experimental models, injection techniques, and pressure definitions, meta-analysis was not considered appropriate. Twenty-eight studies met the inclusion criteria: 12 animal or animal ex vivo studies and 16 human cadaver studies. Intraneural injection was generally associated with higher peak and plateau pressures than perineural injection, but substantial overlap occurred across needle locations. Importantly, low pressure did not reliably rule out intraneural injection, while elevated pressure was also observed during needle-nerve contact and fascial injection. Consequently, the commonly proposed 15-psi threshold showed inconsistent sensitivity across experimental settings. Lower thresholds, including 12 psi, appeared more sensitive in some models but have not been clinically validated. Beyond absolute pressure values, the rate of pressure rise and pressure-time curve morphology showed potential for differentiating needle-tip locations. Injection pressure monitoring may provide a nonspecific warning of needle placement within or against a poorly compliant structure. However, preclinical evidence alone cannot establish whether it should be used routinely or whether it reduces nerve injury. No universal pressure threshold or clinically recommended injection rate can currently be defined.
